questions.q: In a strongly right-skewed distribution of household incomes, which relationship between the mean and median is typically expected?
choices: The mean is greater than the median
The mean is less than the median
The relationship cannot be determined without sample size
questions.answer: In right-skewed distributions, unusually large values pull the mean toward the right tail, making the mean greater than the median.

questions.q: Which summary statistic is considered resistant to extreme outliers?
questions.answer: The median and IQR are based on order statistics/ranks and are resistant to extreme outliers, unlike the mean and standard deviation which incorporate every numeric value.

questions.q: A dataset has values: $3, 5, 7, 8, 9, 11, 15$. If the maximum value $15$ is replaced with $50$, which statistic will NOT change?
questions.answer: The median is the 4th value ($8$). Changing the extreme value from $15$ to $50$ leaves the order and the middle value ($8$) unchanged.

sections.heading: Section 2: The 1.5 x IQR Rule for Outliers

questions.q: A dataset has $Q_1 = 24$ and $Q_3 = 40$. According to the $1.5 \times \text{IQR}$ rule, what are the lower and upper outlier boundaries?
questions.answer: $\text{IQR} = Q_3 - Q_1 = 40 - 24 = 16$. $1.5 \times \text{IQR} = 24$. Lower boundary: $Q_1 - 24 = 24 - 24 = 0$. Upper boundary: $Q_3 + 24 = 40 + 24 = 64$.

questions.q: If a distribution has five-number summary: $\text{Min} = 10, Q_1 = 20, \text{Med} = 28, Q_3 = 35, \text{Max} = 62$, which value is an outlier?
questions.answer: $\text{IQR} = 35 - 20 = 15$. Upper threshold: $35 + 1.5(15) = 35 + 22.5 = 57.5$. Lower threshold: $20 - 22.5 = -2.5$. Since $62 > 57.5$, $62$ is an upper outlier. $10 > -2.5$, so $10$ is not an outlier.

questions.q: What percentage of observations in any distribution lies strictly between $Q_1$ and $Q_3$?
questions.answer: By definition, $Q_1$ is at the 25th percentile and $Q_3$ is at the 75th percentile, so exactly the middle $50\%$ of data lies within the interquartile range.

questions.q: What does sample standard deviation $s$ measure in a dataset?
choices: The typical distance of data points from the sample mean
The distance between the maximum and minimum observations
The difference between the mean and median
The percentage of values that are negative
questions.answer: Standard deviation measures the typical (or average) distance of observations from the arithmetic mean.

questions.q: If every observation in a sample has the exact same value of $14$, what is the sample standard deviation?
questions.answer: When all observations are identical, there is zero variability, so each deviation from the mean ($14 - 14 = 0$) is zero, resulting in $s = 0$.

questions.q: Why is $(n - 1)$ used in the denominator of the sample variance $s^2 = \frac{\sum (x_i - \bar{x})^2}{n - 1}$ instead of $n$?
choices: To make $s^2$ an unbiased estimator of the population variance $\sigma^2$
To ensure the standard deviation is always an integer
Because one observation is always assumed to be an outlier
To adjust for potential measurement errors in the sample
questions.answer: Dividing by $n - 1$ provides degrees of freedom correction so that the expected value of $s^2$ equals $\sigma^2$, making it an unbiased estimator.

questions.q: A boxplot shows a long right whisker, a right-half box wider than the left-half box, and no outliers. What is the shape of the distribution?
questions.answer: An elongated right whisker and a wider upper half of the box indicate that values in the upper $50\%$ are spread over a wider interval, characteristic of a right-skewed distribution.

questions.q: When comparing two test score distributions, School A has $\text{median} = 78, \text{IQR} = 12$ and School B has $\text{median} = 85, \text{IQR} = 6$. Which statement is justified?
choices: School B typically scored higher and exhibited less variability in the middle $50\%$ of scores
School A had a higher maximum score than School B
School A had higher consistency in student scores
School B had more outliers than School A
questions.answer: School B's higher median ($85 > 78$) indicates higher central tendency, and its smaller IQR ($6 < 12$) shows less spread and higher consistency among the middle $50\%$.

questions.q: Which display allows you to recover the original raw data values?
questions.answer: A stem-and-leaf plot retains all individual data values in its stems and leaves, whereas boxplots and histograms bin or summarize data into aggregates.
